searchText: Been staring at that burj khalifa/tower of pisa/screw chart all day. Should gas fees see a similar exponential drop? Could see eth2 as a viable alternative for a lot of transaction-based logs over a bunch of AWS nodes if that's the case Just imagining how cool it would be to yoink aws lambda off our roadmap and start learning Solidity instead. Maybe even update some of our rust macros that autogen a bit of TypeScript for us to build smart contracts Proof of Stake is unlikely to have any significant impact on gas prices. ETH being deflationary would incentivize staking Is it really a deflation but not an "absence of inflation" that matters more? Absence of inflation is deflationary, as your buying power increases over time Buying power increase is generally due to technological advancement But yes, technically, an absence of inflation "the client formerly known as eth2" Deflation is generally considered to be the situation where both incoming and outgoing numbers decrease. Disinflation occurs when the incoming number decreases but the outgoing number does not. (Although there are various disagreements on these terms, because economists.) Following up on this: the "rewards" for being in a sync committee are a significant part of a validator's yearly income. I don't think that having this be down to simple luck is a good thing at all. <@!340345049063882753> said that he didn't like the idea of validators being paid for doing nothing, but in my mind this is by far the lesser evil compared to a system with such high levels of variability on an individual validator's income. And it gives us a reserve pool of "ready and waiting" validators to pull from when the next piece of functionality requires a validator. If you think of the 8/64 reward for non-members of the sync committee as being "was ready to sign but didn't". for members of the sync committee as being "was ready to sign and did", and no reward for "was not ready to sign when required" it doesn't seem so bad. I was asking about two alternatives "power is more or less constant" vs "power increases". Reasoning about the latter would involve quantification on how big the rate of increase is, but the former is either takes place or not. Anyway, this is probably too thin line to worth not talking about much. PSA: https://github.com/eth2-clients/eth2-testnets -> https://github.com/eth2-clients/eth2-networks - See https://github.com/eth2-clients/eth2-testnets/issues/46 for more information For the record I’m pretty comfortable with it either way. Except that we don’t want to have to adjust the balance of every validator every slot because that iteration is expensive. We’d need to fit the not in a committee payments in somewhere that’s efficient which may be possible. Why not simply get rid of the reward, and give a penalty for not participating. You will have the same loop as now with 512 entries The only "reason" I can think to not do it this way is that stakers may be pissed that they miss participating in a slot while in the committee But I'd argue that this is much better than having to move to a pool
